inputs.xtext_rule_text:
InterfaceEnd returns SysML::PortUsage :
	( ownedRelationship += OwnedCrossMultiplicityMember )?
	( declaredName = Name ReferencesKeyword )? 
	ownedRelationship += OwnedReferenceSubsetting
;

notes: The clause prints the header as `InterfaceEnd : PortUsage :`, ending in a second ':' where every sibling has '='. This is the same class of transcription defect recorded by hand on UsagePrefix, DefinitionDeclaration, IncludeUseCaseUsage, FlowDefinition and StateSendActionUsage. It does not change the rule, so no deviation is recorded; whether it is filed on the OMG tracker was not searched, and no issue is cited for it.
decision: A transcription of SysML 8.2.2.14.2. REFERENCES is one of the special lexical terminals of 8.2.2.1.2 and is written out as its keyword alternatives, `'::>' | 'references'`, following the convention used for TYPED_BY and the rest; the Xtext's ReferencesKeyword (SysML.xtext:415) spells the same two literals. The Xtext's `declaredName = Name` against the clause's `declaredName = NAME` is the same position, and NAME is the terminal the specification names, so the token is written as NAME. Nothing else differs. The named-end form is what makes `mqget ::> ...` legal inside an n-ary interface part, where an end needs a name to be referred to later; the binary form usually omits it.

evidence.note: States the production; the rule is its transcription, with the header's stray ':' read as '=' (see notes).
Defines REFERENCES as `'::>' | 'references'`, which is why the terminal is written out as two keyword alternatives rather than referenced.

Lines 78-83 hold six of these ends, each taking the named form: `tlu ::> AHFNorway_LocalCloudDD.TellUConsumer.apisp.APIS_HTTP` is a NAME, then REFERENCES spelled '::>', then the OwnedReferenceSubsetting.
Line 162 `interface differential.rightDiffPort to rearAxle.rightHalfAxle.axleToDiffPort;` has two ends taking the unnamed form: no multiplicity, no name, just the reference subsetting.
Second opinion. Same three parts; its ReferencesKeyword (415) is the same two literals as REFERENCES.
